verdicts.opus: B and D both read the one recorded call and filtered out off-topic labels. Only B set robotics' 14-16x rise against flat AI (1.01x) and the other big topics, and it tied every limit (144-day staleness, top-15 censoring, loose category tagging) to the numbers with a reproducible export. D was correct but narrower and had a coverage-flag inconsistency. A and C measured nothing: A offered labelled memory guesses, and C gave a bare refusal.
verdicts.gpt: C gives the most careful decision-ready reading of the available two-window record: it separates the fastest visible technology-related labels from the off-topic growth leaders, quantifies the comparison, and bounds the stale, loosely categorized feed. B is more expansive and has stronger traced comparison material, but unsupported topic counts and a contradicted coverage claim make it less dependable; neither deliverable achieves usable drill-down.

claude_prism.trend: Both windows are traced, the change is quantified (14.2x, 15.56x, +1.3% for AI) and the dates are stated. Only two points exist, so this is not a true series.
claude_prism.comparison: The baseline is defined, and the deltas and ratios recompute (14893/174 ≈ 85.6). The robotics-vs-AI contrast is meaningful.
claude_prism.chart: The chart is traced, with unit, window, source and caption, and it overlays AI against robotics. Plotting the windows as temporal points at their end dates is slightly awkward.
claude_prism.drilldown: At the ceiling. No follow-up executed and the response exposes no item identifiers.
claude_prism.export: The CSV is traced, carries provenance and a JSON block, and keeps the null growth_x for the new topic. It is a single table.
claude_prism.repro: 87 of 87 numbers trace, derived figures are shown, and a prism-calls block with capture date is included.
claude_prism.accuracy: It catches the off-topic labels, the loose category tagging and a possible clustering artifact. Fields are read correctly.
claude_prism.limits: The 144-day staleness, top-15 censoring, row-floor coverage caveat, label clustering and what the counts are not all sit next to the numbers. It also says what would close the gap.
claude_prism.verdict: The answer is direct and filtered for off-topic labels. It gives a decision and a reasoned low confidence, and names flat AI as contrary evidence.
claude_prism.facets: Rising, newly covered, biggest and window staleness are all grounded. It also addresses label mismatch and the AI-vs-robotics comparison.
